newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian textile exports seen up 10 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian textile exports seen up 10 pct in 1996.

text.p: Indonesia's exports of textile and textile-related products are estimated to hit a total $6.8 billion in 1996, up 10 percent from last year, the Jakarta Post reported on Tuesday.
Minister of Industry and Trade Tunky Ariwibowo was quoted as saying the textile industry was performing better, particularly in its ability to use export quotas.
"Quota distribution and utilisation by textile companies have got better in the last couple of months," Tunky was quoted as saying by the newspaper.
He said in the January-November period, Indonesian textile producers used 74.96 percent of the quota allocated by the United States, up from 63.89 percent in the same 1995 period.
He said Indonesia used 89.55 percent of the quota from the European Union, up from 75.79 percent in the same period last year and 52.43 percent of Canada's quota, up from 50.18 percent.
In September, the government announced it would reduce its textile export target to $10 billion from $12 billion a year until the end of the sixth five-year development plan, which ends in 1999.
